Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 111, verses 1–5:

It is Meccan without any disagreement.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn al-Zubayr and ʿAʾishah, who said: "The verse ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ was revealed in Mecca."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The meaning of tabbat is "perished" (halakat).

Muqatil said: "lost" (kharisat), and it was said: "failed" (khabat).

ʿAṭaʾ said: "went astray" (dallat).

It was said: "emptied of every good" (saffrat), and He specified the two hands for perdition because most work is done with them.

It was also said that by the two hands is meant the self itself, and the hand is sometimes used to express the self, as in His saying: ﴿for what your hands have sent forward﴾, meaning your self. The Arabs often express a part of a thing by the whole, as they say: "The hand of time struck him" and "The hand of death struck him," as in the saying of the poet:

؎When the hand of calamities bore down upon him, he called out: "Is there no informant?"

Abu Lahab's name was ʿAbd al-ʿUzza ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim. His saying "and he perished" (watabba) means he was destroyed.

al-Farraʾ said: "The first is a supplication against him, and the second is a statement of fact, as you say: 'May Allah destroy him,' and 'He has been destroyed.'"

The meaning is that what he was supplicated against has come to pass, and this is supported by the reading of Ibn Masʿud: "and he has indeed perished" (wa-qad tabba).

It was also said that both are statements of fact: by the first he meant the destruction of his deeds, and by the second the destruction of his self.

It was also said that both are supplications against him, and in this there is a resemblance to the general following the specific, although the literal sense of "two hands" is not intended. Allah mentioned him by his kunya because he was well known by it, and because his name, as mentioned above, was ʿAbd al-ʿUzza, and al-ʿUzza is the name of an idol. And because in this kunya there is an indication that he is associated with the Fire, since lahab is the flame of fire. Although the application of that kunya to him originally was because he was handsome, and his face would glow (yatalahhab) with his great beauty, as fire glows.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read lahab with a fatha on the lam and the ha.

Mujahid, Humayd, Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaysin read it with the ha sukun. They agreed on the fatha of the ha in His saying: ﴿a Fire of blazing flame (dhat lahab)﴾. The author of al-Kashshaf narrated that it was read: "Perish the two hands of Abu Lahab," and he mentioned the explanation of this.

﴿His wealth did not avail him, nor what he earned﴾, meaning: what he gathered of wealth did not repel from him what had befallen him of perdition, nor what had descended upon him of the punishment of Allah, nor what he gained of profits and standing. Or the intended meaning of "his wealth" is what he inherited from his father, and of "what he earned" is what he earned by himself.

Mujahid said: "And what he earned" refers to children, for a man's child is part of his earnings. It is also permissible that the "mā" in His saying "mā aghnā" be interrogative, meaning: "What thing availed him?" Likewise it is permissible in His saying "wa-mā kasaba" that it be interrogative, meaning: "And what thing did he earn?" It is also permissible that it be a verbal noun (maṣdariyya), meaning: "and his earning."

The apparent meaning is that the first "mā" is negative and the second is relative.

Then Allah threatened him with the Fire, saying: ﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame﴾. The majority read sayaṣlā with a fatha on the ya, a sukun on the ṣad and a light lam, meaning: "He himself will burn." Abu Rajaʾ, Abu Haywa, Ibn Miqsam, al-Ashhab al-ʿUqayli, Abu al-Simak, al-Aʿmash and Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfaʿ read it with a damma on the ya, a fatha on the ṣad and a shadda on the lam, meaning: "Allah will make him burn." This reading is also narrated from Ibn Kathir. The meaning of ﴿dhat lahab﴾ is "possessing blazing and kindling," and it is the Fire of Jahannam.

﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾ is in conjunction with the pronoun in yaṣlā, and this is permitted because of the separation: meaning, "and his wife will burn in a Fire of blazing flame." She is Umm Jamil bint Harb, sister of Abu Sufyan, and she used to carry thorny ʿaḍā and thorns and cast them at night on the path of the Prophet (ﷺ). This is what Ibn Zayd, al-Dahhak, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas and Murra al-Hamdani said.

Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: she used to walk about spreading slander among the people.

The Arabs say: "So-and-so carries wood against so-and-so" when he spreads slander about him, and from this is the saying of the poet:

؎Indeed the sons of al-Adram are carriers of firewood;
؎they are the tale-bearers in contentment and in anger. ∗∗∗ Upon them is the curse, one after another, and war.

Another said:

؎Of the fair ones who has not hunted upon the back of a coat of mail, nor walked among the people with green firewood.

In this verse he made the firewood "green" (raṭb) because of the smoke in it, which is an increase in evil, and because it matches walking about with slander.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: the meaning of "carrier of firewood" is that she is a carrier of sins and offences, from the saying: "So-and-so gathers firewood on his back," as in His saying: ﴿while they bear their burdens upon their backs﴾ [al-Anʿam: 31]. It was also said the meaning is: "carrier of firewood in the Fire."

The majority read "ḥammālatu" with a damma, as a predicate, the sentence being given to inform that Abu Lahab's wife is a carrier of firewood. As for the reading according to what we mentioned earlier, that "wa-imraʾatuhu" is conjoined to the pronoun in "tuṣlā," the damma on "ḥammālatu" is then an adjective for his wife, and the idafa is genuine because it refers to the past, or it is the predicate of an omitted subject: "She is a carrier."

ʿAsim read "ḥammālata" with a fatha, as a dispraise, or as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl) of his wife.

Abu Qilabah read "ḥāmilata al-ḥaṭab."

﴿Around her neck is a rope of palm fiber (masad)﴾. This clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause of his wife. The jid is the neck, and the masad is the fibre from which ropes are twisted. From it is the saying of al-Nabigha:

؎Hurled with a sinewy, thrusting shaft, its striker ... it has a creak, the creak of a bent bow with its cord.

And the saying of another:

؎O palm-fiber cord, keep away from me, if you are indeed soft, then I am...

Abu ʿUbaydah said: al-masad is a rope made of wool.

al-Hasan said: they are ropes made of a tree that grows in Yemen called al-masad.

Ropes may also be made of camel hide or camel hair.

al-Dahhak and others said: this refers to the world. She used to reproach the Prophet (ﷺ) for poverty, and she would gather firewood with a rope she placed around her neck, and Allah choked her with it and destroyed her. In the Hereafter it is a rope of fire.

Mujahid and ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr said: it is a chain of fire that enters through her mouth and comes out from her lower part.

Qatadah said: it is a necklace of ward (a type of bead) that she had.

al-Hasan said: it was only beads on her neck.

Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab said: she had a precious necklace of jewels, and she said: "By al-Lat and al-ʿUzza, I will spend it on enmity against Muhammad," so that will be a punishment on her body on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-masad: twisting. It is said: "He twisted his rope, yamsudu it, masdan," meaning he perfected its twisting. End.

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "When the verse ﴿And warn your nearest kindred﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 214] was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) went out until he climbed al-Safa and called out: 'Yā ṣabāḥāh!' They gathered around him, and he said: 'Tell me, if I informed you that cavalry were coming out at the foot of this mountain, would you believe me?' They said: 'We have never tried you as a liar.' He said: 'Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.' Abu Lahab said: 'Perish you! Did you gather us only for this?' Then he stood up, and this surah was revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His saying ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ that he said: "They lost."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from ʿAʾishah, who said: "The finest food a man eats is from his earnings, and his child is from his earnings." Then she recited ﴿His wealth did not avail him, nor what he earned﴾ and said: "And what he earned is his child."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His saying ﴿and what he earned﴾ that he said: "His earnings are his child."

Ibn Jarir, al-Bayhaqi in al-Dalaʾil and Ibn ʿAsakir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His saying ﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾ that he said: "She used to carry thorns and cast them on the path of the Prophet (ﷺ) to wound him and his companions." And he said: ﴿the carrier of firewood﴾: "the carrier of tales." ﴿A rope of palm fiber﴾: he said: "They are ropes that exist in Mecca."

It is also said: al-masad is the stick that is in the pulley.

It is also said: al-masad is a necklace of ward.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Zurʿah narrated from Asmaʾ bint Abi Bakr, who said: "When the verse ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ was revealed, al-ʿAwraʾ, Umm Jamil bint Harb, came, with a wail, and in her hand was a stone (fahr), and she was saying:

؎We have disobeyed Muzammam (a name of the Prophet),
؎and we have abandoned his religion, and we have rejected his command.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the mosque, with Abu Bakr beside him. When Abu Bakr saw her he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, she has come and I fear she will see you.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'She will not see me,' and he recited a Qur'an by which he was protected, as the Exalted said: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾ [al-Isra: 45]. She came until she stood over Abu Bakr and did not see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and she said: 'O Abu Bakr, I have been informed that your companion has satirized me.' He said: 'No, by the Lord of the House, he has not satirized you.' So she turned away, saying: 'Quraysh knows that I am the daughter of its chief.'" al-Bazzar narrated it with a similar meaning and said: "We do not know it to have been transmitted with a better chain than this."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from ʿAʾishah, who said: "The finest food a man eats is from his earnings, and his child is from his earnings." Then she recited ﴿His wealth did not avail him, nor what he earned﴾ and said: "And what he earned is his child."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His saying ﴿and what he earned﴾ that he said: "His earnings are his child."

Ibn Jarir, al-Bayhaqi in al-Dalaʾil and Ibn ʿAsakir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His saying ﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾ that he said: "She used to carry thorns and cast them on the path of the Prophet (ﷺ) to wound him and his companions." And he said: ﴿the carrier of firewood﴾: "the carrier of tales." ﴿A rope of palm fiber﴾: he said: "They are ropes that exist in Mecca."

It is also said: al-masad is the stick that is in the pulley.

It is also said: al-masad is a necklace of ward.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Zurʿah narrated from Asmaʾ bint Abi Bakr, who said: "When the verse ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ was revealed, al-ʿAwraʾ, Umm Jamil bint Harb, came, with a wail, and in her hand was a stone (fahr), and she was saying:

؎We have disobeyed Muzammam (a name of the Prophet),
؎and we have abandoned his religion, and we have rejected his command.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the mosque, with Abu Bakr beside him. When Abu Bakr saw her he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, she has come and I fear she will see you.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'She will not see me,' and he recited a Qur'an by which he was protected, as the Exalted said: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾ [al-Isra: 45]. She came until she stood over Abu Bakr and did not see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and she said: 'O Abu Bakr, I have been informed that your companion has satirized me.' He said: 'No, by the Lord of the House, he has not satirized you.' So she turned away, saying: 'Quraysh knows that I am the daughter of its chief.'" al-Bazzar narrated it with a similar meaning and said: "We do not know it to have been transmitted with a better chain than this."
